reference: Independent system ncurses clear for parity; bashclear uses a builtin-presence adapter to select its alias. Escape bytes are captured by the harness, never sent to a terminal. Help and version identities are bash-os contracts.
coverage: xterm visible-screen and scrollback output, including -x preservation
screen and linux terminal capability output
-T terminal override and combined short-option parsing
invalid-option and operand usage statuses compared with ncurses clear
Bash builtin registration, help synopsis, and version aliases
All 22 documented terminal capabilities, ignored private sidecars, shell-local TERM override and dumb status
exclusions: Private PTY attachment and before/after terminal-attribute checks are deferred; the provided runner captures stdout through a pipe.
Custom terminfo databases, serial-line padding, and terminal emulators beyond the listed fixture types are outside this suite.

cases.purpose: Check the common xterm clear sequence, including scrollback clearing, with bytes captured away from a real terminal.
Check that -x preserves scrollback while still clearing the visible screen.
Check the screen terminal's visible-screen sequence, which differs from xterm's erase-display sequence.
Check linux terminal output and clustered -xTTERM parsing while keeping scrollback.
Check that an unsupported terminal name fails without emitting terminal control bytes.
Check the missing-TERM error path and verify that it emits no terminal bytes.
Verify ncurses status 1 for invalid options, capturing all output.
Verify ncurses status 1 for unexpected operands, capturing all output.
Verify ncurses status 1 for a missing -T argument.
Registration and documented synopsis; metadata does not count as operation coverage.
Check both version aliases against the documented bash-os version banner and ensure --help succeeds without producing terminal control output.
cases.stdout:
bashclear 0.1.1 (bash-os; built-in terminal table)
bashclear 0.1.1 (bash-os; built-in terminal table)

cases.purpose: Exercise all 22 documented fixed-table names with/without -x while private tput/terminfo sidecars and unrelated shell dimensions are set; all escape bytes are captured. Include silent dumb failure and shell-local TERM override.
cases.script:
mkdir sidecars
printf 'clear=OVERRIDE\n' > sidecars/xterm
export BASHTPUT_TERMINFO_DIR=sidecars TERMINFO=sidecars TERMINFO_DIRS=sidecars TERMCAP=OVERRIDE LINES=1 COLUMNS=1
TERM=unsupported; export -n TERM
clear -T xterm
clear -x -T xterm
clear -T xterm-256color
clear -x -T xterm-256color
clear -T alacritty
clear -x -T alacritty
clear -T foot
clear -x -T foot
clear -T foot-direct
clear -x -T foot-direct
clear -T xterm-color
clear -x -T xterm-color
clear -T xterm-kitty
clear -x -T xterm-kitty
clear -T screen.xterm-256color
clear -x -T screen.xterm-256color
clear -T rxvt
clear -x -T rxvt
clear -T rxvt-unicode
clear -x -T rxvt-unicode
clear -T rxvt-unicode-256color
clear -x -T rxvt-unicode-256color
clear -T st
clear -x -T st
clear -T st-256color
clear -x -T st-256color
clear -T screen
clear -x -T screen
clear -T screen-256color
clear -x -T screen-256color
clear -T vt100
clear -x -T vt100
clear -T vt102
clear -x -T vt102
clear -T vt220
clear -x -T vt220
clear -T ansi
clear -x -T ansi
clear -T tmux
clear -x -T tmux
clear -T tmux-256color
clear -x -T tmux-256color
clear -T linux
clear -x -T linux
rc=0; clear -T dumb || rc=$?
[[ $rc == 1 && $TERM == unsupported ]] || exit 90

cases.purpose: Verify output to an attached terminal leaves terminal modes and attributes unchanged while producing the selected clear sequence.
cases.reason: The provided fixture runner always captures stdout through a file and has no PTY attachment or termios observation fields. A future isolated PTY fixture should capture bashclear and ncurses clear output, snapshot the PTY attributes before and after each invocation, and compare the captured bytes without connecting to a host terminal.
